meta.coord_system_note: coord_system selects the energy network's input frame on two-shower data only; it does not apply to this experiment.

estimator.name: robust
estimator.label: Robust σ (IQR)
estimator.definition: R = E_est / p per event; σ/E = IQR(R) / (1.349 · median R) per momentum window, in percent, with type-7 quartiles: a σ-consistent width for Gaussian errors that a few badly reconstructed events cannot inflate.

interval.label: 95% percentile bootstrap of IQR(R) / (1.349 · median R) from N = 20, B = 2,000, each replicate's quartiles drawn exactly from its resample's order statistics (sequential conditional Betas), seeded [42, frame, shower, bin, 8] with frames and showers numbered as for the median.

weight.label: Fit weights 1/se², se = c·ŷ/√N recomputed at the fitted value ŷ and iterated, with c the series' pooled scale: the median of √N·κ over its windows of N ≥ 20 from 4 GeV, κ = SE/value each window's bootstrap relative SE. One c per series cancels in the fitted parameters and sets only χ², S and the errors; a per-window κ would put each window's own value back into its weight.

calibration.label: The deposit is c·E_dep with c = Σ p / Σ E_dep per shower over the selection (c_sum), fitted once; it cancels in the robust and sample widths. c_median, 1 / median(E_dep / p) over the events with E_dep > 0, is the calibration the median rel. cross-reference (alt) takes.

estimator.relation: For unbiased Gaussian errors median|R − 1| = 0.6745·σ/E, so a median relative error is quoted beside σ/E, never converted into it.

top.name: Energy (GeV) ⟶
top.rule: E = 1/x², an exact relabelling of the bottom axis; no data are plotted against it.

energy.rule: E = 1/x² of the 1/√E view's x = ⟨1/√p⟩: one exact bijection, so both views draw the same measurements.
notes: The E view's y range follows the windows alone, from zero: those with N ≥ 20 from 2 GeV, whiskers included; a window below 2 GeV never sets it. No fitted curve, band or extrapolation sets it: one that leaves the top is clipped there with a caret.
Fitted curves are drawn from 4 GeV, the lowest window edge any fit can use, to 80 GeV: solid over the windows each fit ran through, dashed beyond, where the curve extrapolates its form.

Each window is drawn at E = 1/x² with x = ⟨1/√p⟩, the abscissa the fits used, so a window on its fitted line in the 1/√E view sits on its fitted curve here; its ⟨p⟩, slightly larger (Jensen's inequality), is in its tooltip.

anchors.rule: Chosen on the whole table's bins, not the selection: the lowest bin from 5 GeV, the highest bin, and the bin between them nearest in log E to the geometric mean of their centres. A series whose anchor is not fittable (N < 20, or no fit weight: tied, no value or a withheld interval) takes its nearest fittable window from 5 GeV in log E, named in substitutions with its cause; with fewer than two, no fit: the robust width has no weaker window to fall back on, and fits no line through one.

model.reason: A single-shower hit experiment carries no reconstruction network, and the XGBoost models read the 59-column aggregate only, so only the detector series is drawn.

substitutions.reason: The nominal anchor 5–6 GeV holds N = 15 for this series, below 20, and no other fittable window from 5 GeV with N ≥ 20 is left: it is dropped.
The nominal anchor 19–20 GeV holds N = 19 for this series, below 20, and no other fittable window from 5 GeV with N ≥ 20 is left: it is dropped.

weight_scale.rule: c is the median of √N·κ over this series' windows of N ≥ 20 from 4 GeV with a fit weight, κ = SE/value each window's bootstrap relative SE (at least 10⁻⁶); the fits weight window k by se = c·ŷ/√N.

notes: The deposit E_dep is the shower's total hit energy in GeV, summed over its cells, and p its incident momentum: one shower per event.

Each window is the producer's integer momentum bin k, [k, k + 1) GeV, of the shower's own momentum. Per event R = E_est / p; the plotted value is the robust σ/E = IQR(R) / (1.349 · median R) in percent, with type-7 quartiles, its whisker the 95% percentile bootstrap of that ratio (B = 2,000, each replicate's quartiles drawn exactly from its resample's order statistics), and its abscissa x = ⟨1/√p⟩ over the window's events. It equals σ/E for Gaussian errors and is not inflated by a few badly reconstructed events; dividing by p event by event removes the window's own momentum spread and the estimator's bias, and c cancels in it, so the detector series does not depend on the calibration.
For unbiased Gaussian errors median|R − 1| = 0.6745·σ/E, so a median relative error is quoted beside σ/E, never converted into it.
The detector series c·E_dep is a linear-sum benchmark, not a limit: a model that reads the shower's shape (leakage, compensation) can do better than a plain sum.
E on both axes is the incident momentum p as the producer writes it. For a massive species √(p² + m²) differs from p by at most m²/2p², 1.7% for a proton at 5 GeV/c.

Robust σ/E is reported, drawn with its whisker, fitted and allowed to set the y range from N = 20 alone, the robust floor: quartiles of fewer events interpolate between single events. A window enters the fits and sets the y range from p ≥ 4 GeV.

Fits: a/√E + b and a₀/√E through the origin, by weighted least squares with weights 1/se², se = c·ŷ/√N taken at the fitted value ŷ and iterated (half steps once the refits oscillate; the first fit takes c·value/√N), with c the series' pooled scale (weight_scale): the median of √N·κ over its windows of N ≥ 20 from 4 GeV with a fit weight, κ = SE/value each window's bootstrap relative SE. One c per series cancels in the fitted parameters and sets only χ², S and the errors; a window's own κ would put its measured value back into its weight, and bias the fits upward. χ², ν = n − p and its p-value. Where χ²/ν > 1 the standard errors and the 95% band are scaled by S = √(χ²/ν) (PDG), and the band then takes Student's t₀.₉₇₅,ν rather than 1.96, since S is estimated from the fit's own ν. The band is the 95% confidence band of the line, not the spread of the events. The quadrature form √(a²/E + b²) is fitted as (σ/E)² = A/E + B and tabled, not drawn; its b and the affine b are different constant terms.

A fit whose residuals average more than 5 of the windows' own standard errors (ν ≥ 1 and S = √(χ²/ν) > 5) has a form that does not describe its windows: it is drawn faded, and said so in its tooltip, the fit table and the drawer. The size of the misfit decides, not the χ² p-value: a window of hundreds of events has so small a standard error that the test rejects a form for misfits no reader could see.

Anchors: the lowest bin from 5 GeV (below it the sampling fraction is still rising), the highest bin and the bin between them nearest in log E to the geometric mean of their centres, chosen on the whole table so they do not move with the selection. A fittable window holds N ≥ 20, lies from 4 GeV and carries a fit weight (a bootstrap SE of at least 10⁻⁶ of its value). A series whose anchor window is not fittable takes its nearest fittable window from 5 GeV in log E instead, and the substitution says why the anchor was not; with fewer than two such windows there is no fit, since the robust width has no weaker window to fall back on. The other mode fits every fittable window from 4 GeV, the 4–5 GeV window included, below the anchors' floor.
The top axis is an exact relabelling of the bottom one, E = 1/x²: a deterministic unit conversion, and no data are plotted against it.
8 of the 10 windows across the series hold N < 20 and report no robust σ/E (the robust floor); Sample σ/μ reports them from N = 2.
Shower: c = Σ p / Σ E_dep = 106 over N = 287 events, fitted once over the whole selection.
Shower: the median rel. cross-reference (alt) takes the median calibration c̃ = 1 / median(E_dep / p) = 62.37, over the 287 events with E_dep > 0.
The shower is not named after a species: the commonest primary particle, e-, covers 24.7% of the 287 selected events; 216 of them have no primary particle, below 95%.
No model series: A single-shower hit experiment carries no reconstruction network, and the XGBoost models read the 59-column aggregate only, so only the detector series is drawn.
Off the axis: 3 windows below 4 GeV (29 events across the series) have x > 0.5; they are listed in off_axis with their σ/E and not drawn.

The y range follows the windows with N ≥ 20 (whiskers included) alone, from zero. No fit sets it: a fit summarises its windows and is not more evidence, so a fitted line or band that leaves the top is clipped there with a caret. 0 windows beyond it are clipped, not rescaled.
